title: BIO 251 ( UNN ) : CHAPTER TWO AND THREE
subject: BIO 251

questions.question: Metabolism is derived from which Greek word?
questions.explanation: Metabolism comes from the Greek word "change".

questions.question: The participating molecules in metabolism are termed which of the following?
questions.explanation: The molecules participating in metabolism are called metabolites.

questions.question: Which structures are completely dead because they do not metabolize?
questions.explanation: Hair and nails are dead parts of an organism because they do not metabolize.

questions.question: Catabolic reactions usually release which form of energy?
questions.explanation: Catabolic reactions usually release energy, often in the form of heat.

questions.question: The chemical energy released during catabolism is often captured in which form?
questions.explanation: The chemical energy released during catabolism is captured in the form of adenosine triphosphate.

questions.question: Anabolism involves the synthesis of molecules and usually requires which of the following?
questions.explanation: Anabolism involves the synthesis of molecules and usually requires energy.

questions.question: Anabolism is a synthetic process in which larger biomolecules are assembled from what?
questions.explanation: Anabolism assembles larger biomolecules from simpler precursors.

questions.question: Catabolic reactions lead to the formation of simpler molecules such as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Catabolic reactions break down complex molecules into simpler ones like urea.

questions.question: Anabolism and catabolism occur simultaneously in the cell but not for which of the following?
questions.explanation: Anabolism and catabolism occur simultaneously in the cell but not for a particular molecule.

questions.question: Which term describes organisms that can use oxygen as an electron acceptor?
questions.explanation: Organisms that can use oxygen as an electron acceptor are called aerobes.

questions.question: Which term describes organisms for which oxygen is obligatory for life?
questions.explanation: Organisms for which oxygen is obligatory for life are called obligate aerobes.

questions.question: Which organism is an example of a facultative anaerobe?
questions.explanation: Escherichia coli is an example of a facultative anaerobe.

questions.question: Which organism is an example of an obligate anaerobe?
questions.explanation: Clostridium botulinum is an example of an obligate anaerobe.

questions.question: Facultative anaerobes can adapt to anaerobic conditions by substituting which of the following?
questions.explanation: Facultative anaerobes can substitute other electron acceptors for oxygen.

questions.question: Which term describes organisms that cannot use oxygen at all and are poisoned by it?
questions.explanation: Organisms that cannot use oxygen and are poisoned by it are obligate anaerobes.

questions.question: Exothermic reactions release energy in which form?
questions.explanation: Exothermic reactions are chemical reactions that release energy as heat.

questions.question: Which term describes exothermic reactions in organisms?
questions.explanation: Exothermic reactions in organisms are called catabolic reactions.

questions.question: Which term describes endothermic reactions in organisms?
questions.explanation: Endothermic reactions in organisms are called anabolic reactions.

questions.question: The joining of amino acids to form a protein is an example of which reaction?
questions.explanation: The joining of amino acids to form a protein is an endothermic anabolic reaction.

questions.question: The breakdown of glucose is an example of which reaction?
questions.explanation: The breakdown of glucose is an exothermic catabolic reaction.

questions.question: Metabolic reactions occur in small steps instead of one large what?
questions.explanation: Metabolic reactions occur in small steps instead of one large explosive reaction.

questions.question: In metabolic pathways, the product of one reaction becomes which of the following for the next reaction?
questions.explanation: In metabolic pathways, the product of one reaction becomes the substrate for the next.

questions.question: A single enzyme generally will catalyze how many reactions?
questions.explanation: A single enzyme generally will catalyze only a single reaction.

questions.question: Enzymes serve to control chemical reactions and ensure they proceed at what rate?
questions.explanation: Enzymes ensure that chemical reactions proceed at an efficient rate.

questions.question: What percentage of glucose energy is released during glycolysis in anaerobic cells?
questions.explanation: About 7% of energy of glucose is released during glycolysis in anaerobic cells.

questions.question: The remaining 93% of glucose energy is harnessed in which cycle?
questions.explanation: The remaining 93% of the energy in glucose is harnessed in the tricarboxylic acid cycle.

questions.question: Aerobic processes in eukaryotic cells occur in which organelle?
questions.explanation: Aerobic processes in eukaryotic cells occur in the mitochondria.

questions.question: Anaerobic processes like glycolysis take place in which part of the cell?
questions.explanation: Anaerobic processes like glycolysis take place in the cytosol of the cytoplasm.

questions.question: Which carrier provides reducing power in the biosynthesis of cell components?
questions.explanation: NADPH provides reducing power in the biosynthesis of cell components.

questions.question: Glycolysis is a ten-step reaction that degrades glucose to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Glycolysis is a ten-step reaction of degradation of glucose to pyruvate.

questions.question: Who discovered the glycolytic pathway?
questions.explanation: The glycolytic pathway was discovered by Gustav Embden and Otto Meyerhof.

questions.question: Glycolysis is also known as which pathway?
questions.explanation: Glycolysis is also called the Embden-Meyerhof pathway.

questions.question: The preparatory phase of glycolysis uses how many ATP molecules?
questions.explanation: In the preparatory phase of glycolysis, two ATP molecules are utilized.

questions.question: The pay-off phase of glycolysis produces how many ATP molecules?
questions.explanation: In the pay-off phase of glycolysis, four molecules of ATP are produced.

questions.question: Which value represents the net yield of ATP in glycolysis?
questions.explanation: The net yield of ATP in glycolysis is two molecules.

questions.question: How many molecules of NADH are produced in glycolysis?
questions.explanation: In glycolysis, two molecules of NADH are produced.

questions.question: In yeast cells, pyruvate is converted to ethanol through which process?
questions.explanation: In yeast cells, pyruvate is converted to ethanol through alcoholic fermentation.

questions.question: In skeletal muscle, pyruvate leads to the production of which of the following?
questions.explanation: In skeletal muscle, pyruvate leads to the production of lactate.

questions.question: In aerobic cells, pyruvate is degraded to which of the following in the mitochondria?
questions.explanation: In aerobic cells, pyruvate is degraded to Acetyl-CoA in the mitochondria.

questions.question: Under anaerobic conditions, pyruvate undergoes which process?
questions.explanation: Under anaerobic conditions, the pyruvate undergoes fermentation.

questions.question: Which enzyme catalyzes the decarboxylation of pyruvate to acetaldehyde?
questions.explanation: Pyruvate decarboxylase catalyzes the decarboxylation of pyruvate to acetaldehyde.

questions.question: The decarboxylation of pyruvate requires which coenzyme?
questions.explanation: The decarboxylation of pyruvate requires thiamine pyrophosphate as a coenzyme.

questions.question: In alcoholic fermentation, acetaldehyde is reduced to which of the following?
questions.explanation: In the second reaction of alcoholic fermentation, acetaldehyde is reduced to ethanol.

questions.question: Which enzyme catalyzes the reduction of acetaldehyde to ethanol?
questions.explanation: Alcohol dehydrogenase catalyzes the reduction of acetaldehyde to ethanol.

questions.question: Homolactic fermentation converts pyruvate to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Homolactic fermentation converts pyruvate to lactate.

questions.question: Where does homolactic fermentation occur?
questions.explanation: Homolactic fermentation occurs in lactic acid bacteria and skeletal muscle.

questions.question: Which enzyme catalyzes the formation of lactate from pyruvate?
questions.explanation: Lactate dehydrogenase catalyzes the formation of lactate from pyruvate.

questions.question: The NADH produced during fermentation is useful at which level?
questions.explanation: The NADH produced is useful at the level of oxidative phosphorylation.

questions.question: Which process regenerates NAD+ for glycolysis to continue?
questions.explanation: The reduction reaction regenerates NAD+ for glycolysis to continue.

questions.question: Which value represents the standard free energy change for lactic acid fermentation?
questions.explanation: The standard free energy change for lactic acid fermentation is -25.1 kJ/mol.
